issues.detail: The Greek 'χειραγωγουντες δε αυτον εισηγαγον' implies that they were 'leading/guiding him' (active action by the others), but the Vietnamese 'dắt tay ông' (taking his hand) adds a specific physical detail ('hand') not present in the Greek text.
The Greek 'ανεωγμενων δε των οφθαλμων αυτου' literally means 'with his eyes not opened'. The Vietnamese 'mắt mở ra' (eyes opened) is the opposite of the Greek meaning.
